episodes.191892: Topical moisture streaming northward into central California triggered another round of afternoon and evening thunderstorms mainly impacting the Sierra Nevada and the Kern County Desert areas. While rainfall amounts were generally a tenth of an inch or less, a  few locations in the south end of the upper Sierra and the Kern River Valley which were impacted by heavier thunderstorms measured over a quarter of an inch of rainfall.
episodes.191918: Hot and very humid conditions with afternoon temperatures in the low 90s and dewpoints as high as 79 degrees at Shelbyville and 77 degrees at Bloomington promoted abundant instability of 3000-4000 J/kg of CAPE, which coupled with adequate wind shear to produce a few late day rotating supercells.  A few reports of 1.00 inch hail were received from Rush, Brown and Decatur Counties, while sub-severe hail fell over northern Johnson County.||More organized and widespread severe weather then approached central Indiana from the west-northwest during the late evening.  This slowly-weakening derecho, which had produced dozens of tornadoes and numerous gusts over 75 mph from eastern Iowa to areas south of Chicago...slowly weakened in a bowing pattern, producing a measured 75 mph gust at Lafayette.  A mixture of tree/power line damage and sub-severe winds then crossed northern portions of central Indiana, with greatest damage in Howard and Hamilton Counties.  Severe winds continued into the first 15 minutes of the 16th (LST) across Marion County, before weakening while continuing to the east-southeast.
episodes.191925: A line of very intense thunderstorms moved from southeast to northwest through the Tucson Metro area. The storm was most intense from midtown Tucson extending to the northwest into portions of Marana. Wind damage was extensive across the much of the Tucson Metro with an estimate of thousands of fallen trees, numerous power poles down, building damage to several buildings, widespread sign damage, roof damage and vehicle damage due to fallen trees. This event also resulted in 1 to 2.5 inches of rain and numerous swift water rescues.
episodes.191927: A weakening line of thunderstorms moved through Massachusetts during the afternoon and evening bringing a smattering of damaging wind reports and sub severe hail.
episodes.191945: A very strong mid level ridge slowly moved through the region, resulting in multiple days of excessive heat. At least one instance of injury and fatality were reported from the heat. The strong ridge eventually shifted far enough east and south of the area to allow sufficient moisture to return, resulting in the development of diurnal convection, with some thunderstorms yielding strong wind gusts.
episodes.191951: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a typical summertime environment. A few trees were blown down.
episodes.191977: A surface trough moved through the Southeast, sparking scattered thunderstorms across the Midlands and CSRA. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging winds and hail (mostly sub-severe).

Nine tornadoes occurred, along with widespread wind damage.  In the City of Chicago, there were 2,810 tree emergency calls and 1,430 calls for tree debris. episodes.192056: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of northwest Indiana during the late evening of July 14th and the early morning of July 15th producing isolated severe winds.
episodes.192057: A line of severe thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the late evening of July 14th producing severe winds and two waterspouts.
episodes.192074: A shortwave trough in a warm and humid air mass allowed for convection across western Pennsylvania to continue tracking eastward across central Pennsylvania during the evening hours of July 15, 2024. Scattered instances of severe thunderstorm wind damage across mainly the northern tier and the Middle Susquehanna Valley occurred before continuing further east into eastern Pennsylvania during the evening hours.
episodes.192092: A teenager performing lawn maintenance was injured by a lightning strike in Altamonte Springs.
episodes.192147: Hot and humid atmosphere allowed for the development of storms along a trough positioned inland. Storms flourished and progressed with outflow boundaries and convergence along the sea breeze. There were some reports of downed limbs and trees. Additional reports of mostly pea sized hail and sub-severe winds were also received.
episodes.192148: Hot and humid atmosphere allowed for the development of storms along a trough positioned inland. Storms flourished and progressed with outflows and convergence along the sea breeze causing some downed trees.
episodes.192427: A stalled front amid an unstable airmass spawned clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms, one of which produced considerable wind damage over far northern Virginia.
episodes.192428: A stalled front amid an unstable airmass spawned clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms, one of which produced considerable wind damage over far northern Virginia.
episodes.192429: A stalled front amid an unstable airmass spawned clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms, one of which produced considerable wind damage over far northern Virginia.
episodes.192439: A couple of thunderstorms produced sporadic gale-force wind gusts over the upper tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.192448: Thunderstorms initiated across central and northern Iowa during the afternoon of July 14th.  A highly unstable and sheared environment quickly led to upscale growth into a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS) that tracked east-southeastward along the northern periphery of a prominent upper-level ridge centered over the southern Plains into the lower Mississippi River Valley.  Widespread wind damage occurred within the path of the MCS during the evening of July 14th into the pre-dawn hours of July 15th...mainly north of the I-74 corridor.  National Weather Service Lincoln damage survey teams found 3 tornado touchdowns along the leading edge of the storms in Marshall County, all 3 of which were rated EF-1. Additional analysis of Sentinel satellite data found two more brief tornadoes occurred in rural Marshall County. These two were rated EF-Unknown.
episodes.192485: A mesoscale convective system (MCS) moved into the Northeast and brought widespread showers and thunderstorms with it. With this system moving into the region in the afternoon and evening, daytime heating helped create an unstable environment. Enough shear was present to support long-lasting storms. In Northeastern Pennsylvania, there were no reports of tornadoes, but there were numerous reports of wind damage ranging from trees being knocked down to roofs being ripped off of buildings. A man, in his home, survived a lightning strike and only suffered minor injuries.
episodes.192590: A surface trough oriented from southwest to northeast stretched across the Piedmont and into southeastern Virginia became the focus for widely scattered shower and thunderstorm activity during the afternoon and evening of July 14th. Activity initially developed in southern Virginia in the afternoon and strengthened as it tracked southeastwards into the Albemarle and Pamlico Sounds during the evening hours, with some of these storms becoming strong in nature and producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192593: Scattered shower and thunderstorm activity developed out ahead of a surface trough located along the Coastal Plain during the afternoon of July 15th. This activity tracked northeastwards across the Neuse River and into the Croatan and Roanoke Sounds with a few of these storms becoming strong in nature producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192763: Increase in instability and PWAT from the southern monsoonal flow produced isolated/dry thunderstorms over northeastern Nevada, causing high wind gusts from outflow boundaries.
episodes.192767: A complex of thunderstorms along a cold front moved across southern Wisconsin causing locally damaging winds, large hail and flash flooding. A tornado occurred near Evansville.
episodes.192782: Scattered thunderstorms developed in a warm and humid airmass that was in place across the Ohio Valley.
episodes.192798: On 13 July, forcing provided by an upper low off the central CA coast, and a southerly flow aloft riding around the outer western periphery of an upper ridge centered over Four-Corners region pulled deep monsoonal moisture northward into the Sierra and western Nevada. These conditions initiated scattered showers and thunderstorms across much of the region. As these weather features showed little movement, a near repeat scenario occurred for 14 July. Showers with embedded storms and lightning lingered through the night into the morning hours. The return of a southwest flow that evening across the Sierra kicked the storms into west central NV with the activity winding down later that night. Residual moisture was slower to scour out the afternoon of 15 July south of US-50 that resulted in a few short lived showers and initiation of pulse-type thunderstorms. The typical array of storm effects included locally heavy rainfall, lightning, outflow gusts of 35+ knots, small hail, and lower CIGS/VIS with mountain obscurations.
episodes.192799: On 13 July, forcing provided by an upper low off the central CA coast, and a southerly flow aloft riding around the outer western periphery of an upper ridge centered over Four-Corners region pulled deep monsoonal moisture northward into the Sierra and western Nevada. episodes.192939: Convection from a passing upper level trough and associated MCS in the morning brought an initial round of non-severe storms mainly in Minnesota into the far reaches of northern Iowa. However, severe weather potential increased by the afternoon as the aforementioned trough and surface boundary made its way into Iowa. Conditions ahead of the boundary included 40-50 knot values of 0-6 km bulk shear, along with 3000-4000J/kg of instability, 25-30 knots of 0-3 km bulk shear and DCAPE values around 1000-1500 J/kg. As a result, a line of showers and storms developed in the afternoon and passed over central Iowa into the evening, with a handful of hail reports in central Iowa generally from penny-size to 2 inches, while the greater majority of reports involved severe wind gusts of 55-70+ mph and associated damage. Tornadic activity within the line of storms did occur, with a tornado developing in the Des Moines Metro area, causing primarily significant tree damage, as well as some structural and power-pole damage in the area as well. Heavy rain given plenty of warm and moist air over the area also resulted in isolated flash flooding, specifically over Black Hawk county.
episodes.192954: A mesoscale convective system (MCS) and an upper-level wave moved through the region triggering widespread showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. These features moved into a high instability environment with sufficient shear in place and plenty of moisture, resulting in a ripe environment for a severe weather outbreak. Damaging wind gusts were the main concern though some storms also had tornadoes. Widespread tree and wire damage occurred across Central New York with two microbursts and two tornadoes surveyed making it one of the most active days of the month.
episodes.192974: Southeast Ohio underwent a heatwave during the middle of July with daily chances of showers and strong thunderstorms each afternoon from the 14th through the 17th. Storms extended down from the Great Lakes region by the peak of the afternoon and brought forth strong enough wind gusts to produce downed trees and power lines. Activity then quickly crossed the Ohio River into West Virginia each evening, bringing the severe weather threat to an end.
episodes.193122: A prevailing SW flow produced a stronger west coast sea breeze that converged with the east coast sea breeze toward the Atlantic coast into the afternoon and evening. Lingering outlflow boundaries also served as convective foci across the area over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.193124: A prevailing SW flow produced a stronger west coast sea breeze that converged with the east coast sea breeze toward the Atlantic coast into the afternoon and evening. Lingering outlflow boundaries also served as convective foci across the area over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.193973: In the late afternoon of the 14th, a line of storms from northeastern Colorado moved southeast through Yuma and Kit Carson counties. This line of storms produced wind gusts up to 65 MPH and blowing dust that reduced visibility down to 0.25 mile.
episodes.193975: In the late afternoon of the 14th, a line of storms from northeastern Colorado moved into northwestern Kansas. This line of storms produced wind gusts up to 61 MPH at the Goodland airport.
episodes.193997: The first of a three-day stretch of hot and humid conditions began on July 15, 2024 across much of eastern New York. Heat indices (or feel-like temperatures) reached between 95 to 104 degrees mainly along the Hudson Valley region. ||The hot, humid environment contributed to the development of a cluster of thunderstorms that impact eastern New York in the evening hours of July 15th. Two broken lines of convection became severe in nature, leading to numerous reports of tree and wire damage in the Eastern Catskills and Mohawk Valley in addition to a few isolated reports in the Upper-Hudson Valley.
episodes.194083: A couple lines of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across southern WI with reports of damaging winds, large hail, and flash flooding. The storms developed along a warm front.
episodes.194189: Another line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across southern WI and moved out over Lake Michigan during an active few days stretch of severe weather.
episodes.194202: A thunderstorm moving through southern Lake Huron produced a wind gust just over 35 knots.
episodes.194236: Severe thunderstorms produced wind damage and heavy rainfall as the storms sagged southeastward across far eastern Iowa on the evening of July 14th.  The strongest storms occurred in Davenport with reports of power outages.
episodes.194238: Severe thunderstorms produced wind damage and heavy rainfall as the storms sagged southeastward across northwest Illinois on the evening of July 14th.  The strongest thunderstorms occurred from the Quad Cities southeastward through Henry County and into southern Bureau and Putnam Counties.
episodes.194278: A deep trough moved into Wyoming and was supportive of numerous showers and thunderstorms. The strongest storms moved through Fremont and Natrona Counties, where wind gusts of over 70 mph were reported. In Hudson, numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. In Lander, a tree was uprooted and fell on a truck. Maximum measured wind gusts included 72 mph near Lander and 70 mph on the east side of Casper. A spotter estimated a wind gust of 77 mph in Bar Nunn.
episodes.194294: An afternoon trough passage supported a few clusters of thunderstorms in an environment characterized by 1000-2000 J/kg of surface-based instability and up to 1500 J/kg of downdraft CAPE. This supported the development of downdraft-aided wind gusts that caused several instances of damage.
episodes.194295: An afternoon trough passage supported a few clusters of thunderstorms in an environment characterized by 1000-2000 J/kg of surface-based instability and up to 1500 J/kg of downdraft CAPE. This supported the development of downdraft-aided wind gusts that caused several instances of damage.
episodes.194324: Thunderstorms rapidly developed over northern Iowa during the afternoon and organized into a powerful line of wind producing storms that surged through the Quad Cities and into northern and central Illinois through the evening hours.  These storms brought widespread damaging winds up to 100 mph for many locations, extending across eastern Iowa, much of Illinois, and into Indiana.  The Storm Prediction Center has classified this event as a Derecho which by definition is a swath of wind damage at least 400 miles long and at least 60 miles wide including several well-separated significant wind gusts over 75 mph.  Corridors of significant wind damage occurred along Highway 20. 10 tornadoes also occurred with these storms in the NWS Quad Cities service area.  ||In addition to the wind, very heavy rainfall fell in a short amount of time with many locations seeing over an inch. Flash flooding was reported in Cedar Rapids as well as in parts of Dubuque County.
episodes.194332: With the subtropical high pressure situated over the Four Corners, the steering flow across AZ was from the southeast. This southeasterly flow advected greater moisture content into the area with PWAT values surging to 1.5+ inches. The moisture combined with the daytime heating resulted in MLCAPE values in excess of 1000 J/KG. A strong to severe thunderstorm complex developed over southeastern portions of AZ by the late afternoon hours and then migrated northwestward toward south-central AZ during the evening hours with outflow winds generating areas of dense blowing dust as well as triggering additional thunderstorm activity over portions of the Phoenix metro area.
episodes.194336: A strong thunderstorm moving across the Bay of Green Bay produced 44 mph wind gusts at Minneapolis Shoal Light during the evening of the 14th.
episodes.194338: A cold front moving through a moist and unstable air mass generated several severe thunderstorms over central Upper Michigan during the evening of the 15th.
episodes.194339: A cold front moving through a moist and unstable air mass produced thunderstorms with heavy rain which caused street flooding in Marquette and Munising on the evening of the 15th.
episodes.194341: A cold front moving through a moist and unstable air mass generated strong thunderstorms over central Lake Superior on the evening of the 15th.
episodes.194342: A strong thunderstorm moving over Minneapolis Shoal produced wind gusts to 39 mph.
episodes.194404: On July 15th, a powerful line of destructive storms moved through portions of the Upper Midwest bringing widespread wind damage to portions of Iowa, Illinois and southern Wisconsin. This storm complex was later classified as a derecho by the Storm Prediction Center. In southern Grant County, the line of storms produced an EF-1 tornado in the town of Kieler in addition to the severe winds.

This storm complex was later classified as a derecho by the Storm Prediction Center. In Clayton County, the storms produced a 75 mph wind gust at North Buena Vista in addition to small hail.
episodes.194473: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours within a typical summertime environment. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.194474: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon hours within a typical summertime environment. A few of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts and hail.

Timing with the MCV corresponded with favorable daytime heating and partly to mostly sunny skies ahead of the system. This resulted in more than 2,000 J/kg of CAPE across much of the region south & southeast of Lake Ontario. Combined with the dynamic nature and the shear associated with the MCV itself, severe thunderstorms developed and moved across the area. ||For the Buffalo forecast area, most of the damage was confined to western New York and the northern Finger Lakes. episodes.194614: An isolated, brief waterspout was observed in association with a convective rain shower well north of Key West.

This led to thunderstorm development in an environment of strong deep layer shear and elevated instability, with multiple supercells occurring. These storms produced very large hail and damaging wind gusts as the storms spread to the southeast. Two storms produced significant damage. The first one produced wind gusts of 80 mph to the northeast of Drake, McHenry County, which combined with ping pong ball size hail to cause extensive damage to crops and property. The second occurred to the south-southeast of Cleveland in which 3.5 inch diameter hail combined with high winds to severely damage two houses and crops in the area.
episodes.194653: Afternoon thunderstorms were able to tap into diurnal energy and summertime moisture. Thunderstorms were able to produce microbursts capable of localized wind damage across central GA.
episodes.194726: Isolated severe thunderstorms produced several reports of damaging wind gusts and an isolated report of hail.

One storm in Cumberland County reported severe wind gusts.
episodes.194756: Evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce 3 funnel clouds over Charlotte and Lee counties.

episodes.194961: Monsoon moisture seeping in from the south fueled isolated thunderstorms, a few of which produced severe weather and flash flooding.

Isolated strong thunderstorms that developed along this boundary brought a single severe wind gust in Knox County. However, the primary impact of this episode was the excessive heat that impacted much of southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa. Heat indices the afternoon of the 15th in this area peaked between 110 and 115 degrees. The highest heat index was 117 degrees, observed by an AWOS station in Harlan, Iowa.
episodes.195208: An area of low pressure centered offshore of southern Oregon and far northern California sent mid-level moisture northward and created an unstable air mass, leading to the development of a severe thunderstorm with strong straight line, downdraft winds in the Rogue Valley cities of Central Point, and Eagle Point. episodes.195211: An area of low pressure centered offshore of southern Oregon and far northern California sent mid-level moisture northward and created an unstable air mass, leading to the development of a severe thunderstorm with strong straight line, downdraft winds in the Shasta Valley city of Montague.
episodes.195222: Increasing moisture associated with a weak monsoonal push led to the development of widespread showers and thunderstorms on the afternoon of the 14th. Widespread street flooding was reported near Gorham Place and Barrington Road and also near 11th Street and Broadway Street.  Significant erosion occurred near roadways and parking lots at the Swedish American Hospital on State Street.  Numerous basements were flooded.
Broken tree limbs.
Reports of downed trees.

Trees were uprooted just east of Esmond Road.  One farm outbuilding was destroyed just east of McQueen Road and the tornado ended in a field just southeast of this location.
A tree was blown down on Parkview Drive.
The Walker Pass RAWS measured 0.52 inches of rainfall between 1900 and 2000 PDT.
The ASOS at the Burlington airport reported an average 5 minute gust of 58 MPH with a peak gust of 64 MPH.
Street flooding in Janesville.

The Agua Fria River gauge near Mayer (AFMA03) began to rise at around 100 AM, rose 2.5 feet by 200 AM, and the dropped to near normal at 1200 PM on the 15th.||There was a Swift water rescue at 835 PM off of Bradshaw Mountain Road in the Quailwood Subdivision (Agua Fria River). Vehicle in the water with two occupants. Report from spotter on social media.
A tree was blown down on Twombly Road, one quarter mile from Woodlawn Road.
Power poles snapped, power lines and trees down in a 2 mile radius around the North Lake area.
Wind gust was measured at the Pamlico Sound WeatherFlow site as thunderstorms were moving through the area.

Numerous trees and tree limbs were blown down between 1st Street and the railroad tracks, just north of Taylor Street.
Roads were blocked due to trees and power lines that were blown down.

Widespread wind damage was reported across southern portions of Cortland including trees, tree limbs and power lines blown down.  Fascia was partly peeled off the police station and the flag pole was bent over.  Fascia was also peeled off of two townhouses.  Southwest facing doors on a small discount store were removed and blown onto Somonauk Road, the doors were locked.  Two campers were rolled over.  Multiple trees were blown down at a cemetery.  Tree and fence damage was also reported along Chestnut Street.
The I-80 at MP 2 Tripod mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 59 mph as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.
A public report via Mping of penny size hail.

The top of a silo was blown off.

A tree was blown down blocking Marcy Road.
A tree and power lines were blown down onto Meredith Road.

A tornado with estimated peak winds of 100 mph touched down just northwest of the intersection of McNulty Road and Meredith Road, where crop damage was evident in high resolution satellite imagery.  The tornado moved southeast producing tree damage and then began moving to the east as it moved through Elburn where trees were blown down and damage occurred to a few farm buildings and houses.  The tornado moved to the east northeast after passing Elburn and destroyed a metal farm building at an equestrian center.  Several trees were blown down and several 2x4 boards were driven at least one foot into the ground.  It is at this location where the tornado was likely at peak intensity.  The tornado ended halfway between Brundige Road and Peck Road, south of Route 38.

A line of severe thunderstorms quickly surged through in late afternoon with a bow echo radar signature to produce damaging winds for much of the area, but a higher end embedded EF1 tornado managed to spin up at a kink in the line where strong rotation was indicated on radar. The tornado took a meandering path through rugged terrain, with discontinuous damage at times from apparent skipping. The first tornadic damage began around Upham Road near Lane Hill in Lincklaen State Forest, and |crossed Hyer and Neal Roads as well. The tornado intensified to higher end EF1 when it reached an exposed ridge along Joe Road, with hundreds of uprooted and snapped large softwood trees in a swath over 200 yards wide. Tree snaps and uproots continued across County Road 13 and then somewhat intensified on the exposed higher elevation of Ridge Road while climbing into Bucks Brook State Forest, before finally dropping into the Otselic Valley to cause additional trunk snaps and uproots. A barn was partially|collapsed, with roof displaced, in Otselic Center. Other structures had minor roofing or window damage from Otselic Center, up Highway 26, to the tornado path ending along Route 80 in Otselic itself where a carport was also lofted. Other pockets of damage such as in Crumb Hill as well as towards South Otselic were more consistent with downbursts from the severe line of thunderstorms.
